thread.title: Kimberly Clark - An Attractive Buy At 52 Week Lows - Kimberly-Clark Corporation (NYSE:KMB)

author: Yanni Lodato
title: Kimberly Clark - An Attractive Buy At 52 Week Lows - Kimberly-Clark Corporation (NYSE:KMB)
text:
Source: Google Images
A look in the consumer defensive sector yields a high dividend paying, in-elastically demanded, and well diversified blue chip stock. Kimberly-Clark ( KMB ) is a cornerstone investment holding for dividend growth and capital protection. KMB holds prominent household brands ranging from Kleenex (tissues), Kotex/Poise (feminine hygiene products), Scott (toilet paper), Huggies/Pull-Ups (diapers), and Depend (underwear). Although KMB does not bring about the enthusiasm and growth potential of tech stocks such as Apple ( AAPL ), Tesla ( TSLA ), and Google (NASDAQ: GOOG ) ( GOOGL ), KMB is a sound investment option for the conservative dividend growth-oriented investor. KMB's growth prospects align closely with population growth as the company's products are indispensable to consumers. Despite negative investor sentiment regarding KBM, I would still rank the stock a buy as a result of the company's steady product demand, 45 years of dividend growth, and encouraging growth prospects.
Why Buy Kimberly-Clark? Dividend- KMB offers an attractive dividend yield of 3.81%. Furthermore, KMB has overseen 45 years of consecutive dividend increases and KMB's payout ratio of 57.6 is moderate. KMB exhibits all the markings of a venerable and stable company with both the desire and ability to reward shareholders.
KMB Dividend data by YCharts
Business Advantages- KMB is globally diversified across 175 countries worldwide, manufacturing a wide selection of consumer products ranging from paper towels, tissues, diapers, and more. KMB's operating segments are diversified across the personal care, consumer tissue, and professional segment. Kimberly-Clark's personal segment of Huggies, Pull-Ups, Kotex, Depend, and Poise comprises nearly half of annual sales, the consumer tissue segment made up of Kleenex, Scott, Cottonelle, and Viva make up a third, and the remainder is derived from the professional segment. All of KMB's products are steadily demanded by consumers regardless of economic vagaries, assuring continued product demand and capital protection over the long run. KMB is boring but in a good way. In relation to the broader market KMB experiences very little volatility as it is unlikely that any disruptive changes will occur in the personal paper products segment. KMB benefits from a number of economic advantages; the company can leverage store space in retailers such as Target, Walmart, Costco, etc., KMB derives cost advantages because of the company's large-scale, and KMB products elicit brand loyalty and multi-item sales (once parents find a particular diaper that works they are likely to stick with it and large companies are inclined to use just one brand for their toilet paper dispensers, soap, paper towels, etc.). Furthermore, the KMB brand benefits from strong consumer recognition. KMB has a very large product selection and the company's Kleenex brand has even become a household name (ex. Can I have a Kleenex?).
Management - KMB has exhibited good managerial oversight. KMB's current management team has presided over $450 million in cost mitigation efforts (of an anticipated $2 billion), 2% organic sales growth in 2018, share buybacks, elevated EPS numbers, and a strong commitment to cost suppression efforts. KMB has also witnessed margin expansion as a result of management's increased focus on the company's bottom line. Additionally, KMB's executive compensation plan closely aligns executive performance with shareholders. According to the most recent annual report , 50% of the CEO's pay was derived from stock options and additional monetary rewards were based on financial improvements ranging from ROIC and annual net sales growth.
KMB Profit Margin (Annual) data by YCharts
Valuation- KMB is priced at a more moderate valuation; the company's PE ratio of 16 is close to the moderate benchmark of 15 and KMB is fairly valued based on intrinsic cash flows: KMB's current share price of $104 is below the KMB's future cash flow value of $115. KMB is also trading at a share price close to $100, a share price not seen since 2014.
Concerns Regarding Kimberly-Clark Despite KMB's business and investment advantages, the company faces a number of issues ranging from KMB's long-term debt load of $7.4 billion, top-line revenue decreases, incremental growth, and depressed advertising spending. Over the past number of years, KMB has experienced top-line revenue contraction of close to $2.5 billion.
KMB Revenue (Annual) data by YCharts
Source: Statista Kimberly-Clark Advertising Spending
Depressed annual revenues have coincided with falling advertising spending, notice KMB's revenues are at their highest during peak advertising and sequentially fall lower as advertising spending is curtailed.
Source: Kimberly-Clark Advertising Spending 2011-2017
Depressed revenues are also likely a result of the changing consumer climate toward digital e-commerce sales and renewed product innovation by peers (ex. P&G's penetration into the incontinence market and now preeminent market share in the diaper segment).
However, KMB still benefits from its $1 billion in product innovation and marketing expenditures, large bargaining power with major retailers, and focus on efficiencies ranging from cost elimination to divestitures from unprofitable operations (ex. Western & Central European diaper business, the spin-off of its consumer healthcare business, etc.) KMB's revenues are reflective of new market challenges; in particular, now there is a more diverse consumer product selection online necessitating that KMB elevates advertising to stay competitive and expand revenues. I anticipate revenue losses to be temporary as over the long term revenue declines will be mitigated by elevated advertising spending, an increased online presence, and continued population growth especially in emerging markets such as China, Brazil, and India. In 3rd quarter 2017, KMB noted that revenues derived from developing and emerging markets grew 3% year-over-year. Furthermore, the global middle-class population is set to increase by 1.92 billion people by 2030 offering a steady growth trajectory for KMB's consumer defensive product line.
One other aspect to take into consideration is KMB's large debt load. The company's long-term debt has accumulated to $7.4 billion. Although KMB's debt levels are covered by operating cash flow (39.2% coverage, greater than 20% of debt); the company's highly leveraged balance sheet is a consideration for the conservative investor.
KMB Total Long Term Debt (Annual) data by YCharts
Conclusion Despite debt and revenue concerns, KMB remains well positioned for long-term success. Despite short-term revenue fluctuations, KMB's growth trajectory in emerging markets and global middle-class population growth will assure future revenue growth. KMB displays a number of business advantages. KMB exhibits a management committed to shareholder value, cost reduction, margin expansion. Furthermore, the company's products are subject to inelastic demand and KMB boasts an extensive product selection. KMB also offers appeal from an investment perspective as a result of the company's more moderate valuation, consistent dividend increases, and history of capital appreciation. Additionally, as markets cool down, KMB will offer a good momentum trading opportunity as investors readjust portfolio holdings to more defensive stock options.
